question.prompt: Which of the following is equivalent to “If \(P\) is true then \(Q\) is false”?

solutions.explanation:
An if-then statement is false exactly when its hypothesis is true and its conclusion is false. Therefore, “If \(P\) is true then \(Q\) is false” is false exactly when \(P\) and \(Q\) are both true.

Choice D, “If \(Q\) is true then \(P\) is false,” is false in exactly the same situation. In every other truth assignment, both conditionals are true. Thus they are equivalent. Choice D is the contrapositive of the original statement, so the answer is D.
solutions.title: Compare when the statements are false
